resolves: concurrency scope of the opt-in admission path
decisions: Do not change submit_job(). Add a separate opt-in public operation named submit_job_admitted(command, max_queued_jobs=...).

max_queued_jobs is supplied explicitly by the caller/configuration owner; this lab does not invent a global production threshold. Its contract domain is a non-negative integer; a negative value is rejected with ValueError before any job/id side effect.
The public result is machine-readable: accepted returns {accepted: true, job_id: ...}; overload returns {accepted: false, code: OVERLOADED}. Human-readable text is not the contract discriminator.
Rejected overload creates no Job and consumes no job id.

Concurrent calls through the admitted path must serialize admission-check plus job creation against each other. Legacy submit_job() intentionally bypasses admission and is outside this opt-in guarantee.
Worker claims may reduce queued work concurrently; that can make the admission decision conservative, but must not cause over-admission among admitted submissions.
The M11 SLO target and denominator are unchanged. Rejected work is reported as admission rejection, not reclassified as successful accepted work.
new_authority_grant: implementation_agent may implement the above semantics inside the existing allowed write scope
implementation_agent may add local synchronization required only for the admitted submit operation
implementation_agent may add focused regression tests
